name: Tunisian Chakchouka (Eggs in Spiced Tomato & Pepper Sauce)
why: Peak tomato season in the UK right now, and chakchouka is the North African way to put them to work — a rustic Tunisian skillet dish of spiced tomato and peppers with eggs poached right in the sauce. One pan, hands-off simmer, and it works for breakfast, lunch or dinner.
ingredients: 4 ripe tomatoes, diced (or 2 x 14oz cans, lightly drained)
¾ tsp salt, plus more to taste
Crusty bread or pita, to serve

steps: Dice the onion, slice both peppers, mince the garlic and dice the tomatoes (drain them if using tinned).
Line up your spices — cumin, paprika, chilli powder and salt — ready to add all at once.
In a large cast-iron skillet or sauté pan with a lid, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add the peppers and garlic and cook for a further 3-5 minutes until the peppers start to soften.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt and chilli powder. Mix well and bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low.
Simmer, uncovered, for 10-15 minutes until the sauce has thickened to your liking. Taste and adjust the salt and chilli.
Using the back of a spoon, make four craters in the sauce, each large enough to hold an egg.
Crack one egg into each crater.
Cover the pan and simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Slide the whole pan to the table or spoon the chakchouka onto plates.
Serve immediately with crusty bread or pita for mopping up the sauce and yolks.

pro_tips: Use a cast-iron pan and serve it straight from the skillet — the whole point of chakchouka is communal sharing with bread straight off the pan.

If you have a really good ripe tomato, halve it instead of dicing so pieces break down slowly and the sauce stays chunky. Swap half the bell pepper for a charred Aubergine for a fuller North African version.
author: Henry
